critique.good: Crop column at 170 keeps every crop and variety label on one line; the date pair is close in width (150/145) and reads as a timeline; no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: Comments are the tallest cells, about 8–10 lines, and force a 1138px table; columns 1–3 have large dead space under short entries. The yield column at 85 is too tight: its header breaks into three lines and the numeric ranges are cramped, slowing comparison.
critique.cause: Only 169px, or 148px of text, is left for the 1035px comment content, while 465px goes to crop plus dates. Yield needs 129px to keep its 108px range/header intact; at 85px it gets 64px of text, so it must wrap.

critique.good: Date columns are the most generous (175/170) and nearly equal, so the sowing and harvest ranges are easy to read; the crop column still leads visually.
critique.problems: Crop at 140 is below the 149px one-line width, so labels like বোরো ধান (উফশী) and সরিষা (বারি সরিষা-১৪) wrap and row identifiers no longer scan as units. Comments at 154 are even more starved than r0A, producing 9–12 lines and a 1301px table, with large empty areas in the wide date columns.
critique.cause: Width priority is inverted: 345px is spent on the date pair while comments get 154px and crop gets 140px. Text areas are 119px for crop, below 149px, and 133px for comments, so both wrap heavily while dates have unused space.

critique.good: Most compact (836px) and best overall rhythm. Crop at 170 preserves identifiers, comments at 239 are the most readable, and row heights are more even.
critique.problems: The date columns at 120/115 are too narrow: date ranges break into 3–4 short lines and the paired timeline becomes ragged. Yield at 75 splits every value into two lines and its header into three. Comments still set row height (row 1 is about 8 lines), so the tight dates are not buying a proportional height reduction.
critique.cause: 239px to comments plus 170px to crop leaves only 235px for both date columns and 75px for yield. Date text areas are 99/94px against one-line needs of 263/239px; yield text area is 54px against 108px, so values split at the dash.

critique.good: Crop column 170 keeps most crop and variety labels on one line, and the paired date columns 135/130 are close enough to scan together. Yield values stay intact, with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: Comments at 199px are the height driver: 6–7 lines, a 999px table, and large empty blocks under crop/date/yield in rows 1, 4, 5 and 6. Row heights are uneven and the table feels loose. The yield column gets 85px while comments are starved.
critique.cause: Too much width is assigned to crop (170) and yield (85), and too little to comment (199). Comment text is by far the longest content, so every 10px there changes several rows.

critique.good: The most compact version: comment width 224 reduces line count, the table is 883px, and row heights are more even at 129–153px. Crop at 160 still keeps most identifiers on one line, with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: Date columns 130/125 are slightly tight, producing 3-line date cells in rows 1–2. Row 4 crop name wraps because 160 is below its one-line need. The yield header still wraps to 3 lines. The date pair is also slightly asymmetric.
critique.cause: Crop 160 and yield 80 consume width that could go to the date pair; comment 224 is good but not generous. The 130/125 split is not quite balanced for a paired timeline.

critique.good: The widest date columns, 145/140, make sowing and harvest text easiest to compare. Crop at 170 keeps identifiers intact, with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: Comment column 184 is far too narrow: comments reach 7 lines, the table grows to 1069px, and rows 1, 3, 4 and 6 have large empty areas in the first four columns. The table looks inflated and slow to scan.
critique.cause: Allocating 170+145+140+80=535px to the first four columns leaves only 184px for the very long comments. Comment wrapping then dominates every row height.

critique.good: Clean, even rhythm from row 4 down (all 129px), and the sowing/harvest pair (132/128) reads as a genuine pair. No mid-word breaks, yield column compact and unobtrusive.
critique.problems: The comment column is visually dominant — nearly 1.8× each date column — so the page reads as an essay with dates attached rather than a schedule comparison. Six-line comment in the বোরো row makes that row 153px, a heavy outlier that breaks the otherwise steady 129px rhythm. The header 'ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)' breaks into three lines, giving a tall, spindly header over a one-line numeric column.
critique.cause: col 5 at 229px leaves only 208px of text width, which is exactly what forces 5–6 line comments (বোরো, পাট, গম). col 4 at 80px leaves 59px, below the ~108px one-line header width, hence the 3-line header. col 1 at 150px leaves 129px, under the 149px one-line crop width, so every crop name wraps to two lines.

critique.good: Best total height (836px) and the only design where a row (পাট) drops to 106px; the extra 10px of comment width is visibly repaid in the মন্তব্য column, which reads as calmer 4-line paragraphs.
critique.problems: The date pair is asymmetric (130 vs 125): the harvest column is narrower and wraps earlier, so side-by-side comparison of sowing vs harvest looks slightly skewed, and the ragged right edges of the two columns don't line up. Crop column at 145px still wraps every name.
critique.cause: col 3 at 125px gives only 104px of text — the tightest in any design — while col 2 gets 109px; the 5px difference crosses a wrap threshold in the গম and সরিষা rows. col 1 at 145px (124px content) is still below the 149px needed for one-line crop names.

critique.good: Widest, most comfortable date columns (135/130), so the sowing and harvest phrases wrap into clean 3-line blocks and are easy to compare row to row; comment text lines are still readable.
critique.problems: Tallest table (883px) with no row below 129px — a uniform wall of 5-line comments. The comment column is squeezed to 224px while the date columns are the widest of all three, an imbalance that trades away the very thing that controls table height. The overall block feels dense and monotonous.
critique.cause: col 5 at 224px yields 203px of text, just under the threshold that lets several comments finish in 4 lines, so বোরো/আমন/গম/সরিষা/পাট/মসুর all land on 5–6 lines; meanwhile the 135/130 date widths buy no reduction in date-column line count (still 3 lines).

understanding.purpose: Compare crops by their sowing and harvest windows, yield index, and accompanying notes in a seasonal schedule.
understanding.reading: Row by row: identify the crop in column 1, compare the paired sowing and harvest timing in columns 2–3, read the yield in column 4, then consult the comment in column 5.
groups: Columns 2 and 3 form a paired sowing–harvest timeline and should have similar widths so the two dates can be compared across rows.
Column 4 is a compact numeric attribute attached to the timing pair and needs much less width than the date columns.
Column 1 is the row identifier and should stay strong; column 5 is secondary commentary whose width depends on whether notes or schedule comparison is prioritized.
keep_intact: Crop names and variety identifiers such as বোরো ধান (উফশী), আমন ধান (স্থানীয়), গম (বারি গম-৩৩), সরিষা (বারি সরিষা-১৪)
Numeric yield values and the unit টন/হেক্টর
Month names and date words, which may wrap at spaces but must not break mid-word
may_wrap: Sowing and harvest date ranges in columns 2–3 at natural word spaces
Longer crop names only at spaces or parentheses if the crop column is tightened

bad.why: r1C gives the crop and date columns 170/145/140px while leaving the long prose column only 184px, so comments wrap to 7 lines and the table grows to 1069px. The hierarchy is inverted: the free-text column is narrower than the date columns, making the table slow to scan and unnecessarily tall.

final.rationale: r3B treats the table as a calendar: the crop/date block stays just wide enough to avoid mid-word splits and keep row headers readable, while the residual width goes to the prose column where it prevents the most line growth. The result is a compact 743px table with calm, mostly uniform 106px rows; no column looks starved, and the numeric yield column remains a narrow, easily compared strip. r1C inverts that hierarchy by giving the date columns more width than the comment column, producing 7-line cells and a 1069px table.

general: Allocate width by role: row headers need scan width, numeric columns can be narrow, and the free-text column should absorb residual width.
Check line-break thresholds: a few pixels can remove an orphan line, but past that point extra width in short columns buys little.
Uniform row heights and intact words matter more than making the table as short as possible.
A narrow numeric column with a wrapped header is often better than widening it at the expense of prose.
specific: In this Bengali crop calendar, column 1 needs about 124–136px, columns 2–3 about 120–130px, column 4 about 74–88px, and column 5 about 250–270px.
r3B's 128/124/122 crop-and-date block is close to the compression limit before date phrases become noticeably choppy.
The 80px yield column is sufficient because the values are short ranges and the header can wrap to three lines.
r1C's 184px comment column is the specific failure: it is narrower than the date columns despite holding the longest text.

final.tradeoffs: r3A and r2B give more breathing room to the crop and date columns and may read more comfortably at a glance, but they add 70–93px of height and less uniform rows. r3B accepts some 4-line date cells in order to keep the prose column dominant.
final.uncertain: Whether the 128px crop column is too tight for row-header scanning; some designers would prefer r3A's 134px and accept the extra height. Exact Bengali line-break thresholds around 124–130px are also renderer-dependent.

A.why: Equal column widths leave the yield column mostly empty and squeeze the long comments into many short lines. The resulting tall rows make comparisons harder.

B.why: Crop names and yield ranges stay intact, and the wider comments column gives the rows a useful rhythm. The yield heading wraps awkwardly over three lines.

C.why: The wide comments column reads comfortably, but several crop names wrap and the first two yield ranges split across lines, disrupting numeric comparison.

D.why: Comments have room to read and yield ranges remain on one line. Several crop names and the yield heading wrap, and the sowing column is somewhat cramped.

E.why: Crop names and yield ranges stay intact, with well-matched widths for sowing and harvest. Comments are narrow and create tall rows with considerable empty space elsewhere.

F.why: Sowing and harvest have similar widths, yield ranges stay intact, and comments read reasonably well. Several crop labels wrap and the yield heading takes three lines.

reviews.unsure: B offers the strongest balance between intact row labels and readable comments, though its narrow yield heading is awkward; D and F give comments slightly more room at the cost of wrapping more crop labels.

A.why: The crop labels mostly stay on one line, the two date columns have similar proportions, and the notes have enough width to read comfortably. The yield heading wraps to three lines.

B.why: The equal-width columns leave too much space for the short yield values and squeeze the notes into very narrow, heavily wrapped lines. Tall rows and large empty areas make comparison harder.

C.why: The date columns are balanced, yield ranges stay intact, and the notes read comfortably. Several crop labels wrap, and the yield heading occupies three lines.

D.why: The wider notes are easy to read, but the first two yield ranges break across lines, making numerical comparison harder. The crop and date columns also feel cramped.

E.why: The notes have a generous measure and yield ranges remain on one line. Crop labels and several date phrases wrap, including a four-line sowing entry, but rows remain readable.

F.why: Crop labels stay intact and the date columns support comparison well. The narrower notes wrap heavily, making rows tall and leaving substantial empty space in the other columns.

reviews.unsure: A, C and E make different reasonable tradeoffs between keeping crop labels together and giving notes more room. A's three-line yield heading is a noticeable compromise.
